description.narrative:
The projects overarching goal is to improved environmental health and resilience of WASH-deprived urban poor living in slums and low income settlements.
To achieve this goal, the expected outcomes of the project are:
Outcome-1: WASH deprivation reduced among target communities through increased WASH awareness and access to climate resilient WASH services
Outcome-2: Local governance in pro-poor WASH service delivery and coordination with other services in target cities and towns improved
Outcome-3: WASH policies and strategies improved in favour of urban poor through evidence and advocacy

Den växande befolkningen boende i slumområden som följd av framförallt den snabba urbaniseringstakten i Bangladesh, har idag en mycket begränsad tillgång till kvalitetssäkrad vatten- och sanitet. Avsaknaden av statlig vatten-, sanitet- och hygienreglering kombinerat med svaga leverantörer inom sektorn ökar bland annat befolkningens sårbarhet mot vattenburna sjukdomar och andra miljörelaterade risker kopplade till katastrofer och översvämningar. Bristerna inom vatten och sanitet har också en stor negativ inverkan på nutrition, hälsa och utbildning. Dessa specifika utmaningar som drabbar den fattiga befolkningen i urbana slumområden kräver lösningar på individ-, kommunal-, institutionell- och politisk nivå. WaterAids föreslagna insatser för att förbättra tillgängligheten till vatten och sanitet i vanligtvis försummade slumområden ligger i linje med övergripande mål i den svenska regeringens strategi att skapa förutsättningar för bättre levnadsvillkor för människor som lever i fattigdom och under förtryck. Insatsen tar en integrerad, tvärsektoriell ansats och kan genom detta bidra till synergier mellan Sidas resultatområden inom resultatstrategin för Bangladesh 2014-2020: i) demokrati, jämställdhet och mänskliga rättigheter, ii) bättre möjligheter för människor som lever i fattigdom iii) bättre miljö, begränsad klimatpåverkan och ökad motståndskraft och iv) förbättrad grundläggande hälsa. Både resultatstrategin och Sidas policyram för svenskt utvecklingssamarbete och humanitärt bistånd understryker vikten av tillgången till hållbara och resilienta vatten- och sanitetsinrättningar i dess betydelse för att förbättra grundläggande hälsa, särskilt mödra-l och barnhälsa, vilket är bevisat betydligt sämre i slumområden jämfört med icke-slumområden. Insatsens arbete med att förbättra vatten och sanitet hos vårdinrättningar samt att ge utbildning till primärhälso- och sjukvårdspersonal bedöms också bidra till att stärka vårdsystemen generellt. Den föreslagna insatsen kommer att fokusera på att på kommunal nivå hjälpa regeringen i Bangladesh och olika lokala myndigheter att förbättra miljö, hälsa och resiliens genom förbättrad vatten- och sanitet hos befolkning boende i slumområden låginkomstområden. För att uppnå detta mål är de förväntade resultaten av projektet: • Vatten- och santitetsbrister minskas bland målgrupper genom ökad vatten- och sanitetsmedvetenhet samt genom ökad tillgång till klimat- och katastrofresilienta samhällstjänster kopplade till vatten- och sanitet; • Lokal förvaltning vid leverans och styrning av vatten- och sanitet, vilket även samordnas med andra samhällstjänster i städer ska och har förbättrats med avseende på vatten och sanitet; • Strategier kopplade till vatten och sanitet skall förbättras till förmån för de fattiga i städerna genom evidensbaserat arbete kombinerat med juridiska medel. Sverige bidrar med 55 MSEK av insatsens totala budget på ca. 67 MSEK under perioden 2018-2022. Insatsen beräknas nå och gynna 450 000 innvånare boende i 170 olika slumområden i Dhaka, Chittagong och Khulna tillsammans med ytterligare tre städer i andra delar av landet.

The proposed project will support the different local government institute of Government of Bangladesh to improve environmental health and resilience of WASH-deprived urban poor living in slums and low income settlements. To achieve this goal, the expected outcomes of the project are: • WASH deprivation reduced among target communities through increased WASH awareness and access to climate/disaster resilient, community-based WASH services • Local governance in pro-poor WASH service delivery and coordination with other services in target cities and towns improved • WASH policies and strategies improved in favour of urban poor through evidence and advocacy

description.narrative:
Examples of Results Achieved (WASH for Urban Poor with WaterAid Bangladesh)
This conclusion on performance has been developed after the end of the fourth year (January-December 2021) of five-year contribution WASH for Urban Poor with WaterAid. The project aim is to improve environmental health and resilience of WASH deprived urban poor living in slums and low-income settlements in 3 big cities including Dhaka, Chattogram and Khulna and 3 municipal towns of Sakhipur, Saidpur and Paikgachha. The contribution is now in its fifth year, and WaterAid Bangladesh, along with its implementation partners, is committed to achieve the targeted goals in three main areas: A total of 33,225 people received access to clean water during this reporting period, and 37,294 people benefited from improved sanitation services in the project areas consisting of low-income communities, educational institutes, and Health Care Centers (HCF).
By constructing gender friendly toilets, raising awareness of the women and girls in the communities and schools on MHM issues, the activities were found to be gender inclusive which are contributing to SDG 5 & SDG 10, along with SDG 6, which is coherent with the project's activities. Additionally, WASH4UP project addresses other SDGs like 3, 4 and 11 through its various interventions.
To ensure the long-term sustainability of WASH facilities, a total of 418 caretakers have been trained on the operation, maintenance, and management of the WASH facilities. Apart from that, the project has generated WASH funds in which the community and the institutions have demonstrated self-ownership and deposited around 10-20% of the total installation/ construction cost of the WASH facilities, based on their economic capability for post implementation sustainability. Over the reporting period, more than BDT 5.44 million was mobilized as local WASH fund, to be used in the coming years for the operation and maintenance (O&M) of the WASH facilities.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, hygiene has been given special importance in the reporting year as well. During this time, 64,969 people were directly reached with handwashing messages at community level.
A total of 54,603 women and adolescent girls received awareness messages on Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) through different events and one to one counselling with informative printed materials.
Through a total of 3,102 events organized by the hygiene volunteers, people received messages on water safety plan and how to keep the shared facilities safe. In addition, 1,000 hand-washing facilities have been installed and/or renovated at households and institutions by enhancing household and community level motivation and project fund. This enabled people to have access to improved hand-washing habits. Moreover, awareness-raising messages on hygiene has been disseminated, aligning with COVID-19 protocols for this year.
The project activities have enlightened the community people with the importance of washing hands properly at different times and has changed the handwashing practices of community people and targeted beneficiaries into a positive direction compared to the pre-project intervention situation. According to the findings of the baseline study, majority of the community people did not have proper handwashing facilities at home; neither did they have the awareness to wash hands with soap. However, the midline study findings were different and stated that community people have become aware and are practicing proper handwashing with soap, at correct times.
The project also continues to provide O&M support to 30 public toilets which recorded more than 3.08 million uses which was further complemented by 48 spot & event based mobile toilets during the reporting period. Since the beginning, the project has provided support to the construction, O&M of fecal sludge management (FSM) plant in Saidpur municipalities. Apart from this, construction of another FSM plant in Sakhipur Municipality of Tangail district has also been completed and is currently fully functional. During this reporting period, 1,371 latrine pits/septic tanks were emptied and treated duly, following the health and safety policy of WaterAid. As a part of this initiative, waste bins have been distributed to 419 households in the selected municipalities to establish an organized collection system. On the other hand, at city corporation level, 02 community based Solid Waste Management (SWM) systems were developed for supporting additional 1,008 households in low-income communities. A total of 2,778 households were motivated into safe disposal of child faeces during this time.
As a part of sector capacity building initiatives, international training on faecal sludge and septage management, learning visits, meetings and workshops have been organized for different duty bearers and other stakeholders, including project implementing partners. In addition, the project collaborated with institutions representing cross-cutting sectors such as education, health, and agriculture through 130 meetings and 14 workshops to ensure sustainable WASH services.
As a key WASH player in Bangladesh, pre and post online budget advocacy conference have been organized for influencing the government to fill up the financial gap in WASH sector to achieve SDG6 and particularly, address the COVID-19 situation.
WaterAid has been engaged at national level to raise awareness among relevant authorities on improved urban WASH policies and strategies, including water efficiency, progressive tariffs, pro-poor allocation, FSM and urban rainwater harvesting through sector capacity building and mass campaigning. The project, in collaboration with the education departments of Khulna, Dhaka (North & South), and Chattogram arranged 05 workshops to make school authorities aware of COVID- 19 issues as a part of the school preparedness activities.
Furthermore, in the continuation of advocacy works with Water Supply and Sewerage Authority (WASA), the project personnel regularly engaged in the central and zonal level planning meetings with WASA. During the reporting period, a total of 30 central and zonal coordinating meetings with WASA officials were arranged. As a result, 103 additional water points were legalized during this time.
WaterAid Bangladesh is actively involved with Policy Support Branch (PSB) of Local Government Division (LGD) to draft the National Policy on Public Toilet construction, operation and management in Bangladesh. Other likeminded stakeholders working with public toilets in Bangladesh are also involved in the process.
A study on water utilities in selected urban municipalities in Bangladesh has been completed under the project during the reporting period. The findings will be shared among the stakeholders in collaboration with Municipal Association of Bangladesh (MAB).
